reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the output contract, resource assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, Evidence resource-review context, full Evidence StructureDefinition report, the direct SearchParameters behavior finding whose `affectedResources` include `Evidence`, shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior context, and the local R4/R6 Evidence StructureDefinitions. I used the deterministic aggregate only as prior context and compared it after forming the resource-level judgment. Shared base behavior findings were considered only as ecosystem context because this review is for `Evidence`, not `Resource` or `DomainResource`.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Evidence was trial-use/FMM 0, so the baseline standards pressure to preserve the exact R4 wire model is weak. That makes the R6 variable/statistic redesign easier to justify than it would be for mature or normative content, but it does not eliminate compatibility value where the break affects every valid R4 instance, evidence interpretation, repository metadata, or low-cost conformance aliases.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Evidence keeps its R6 resource identity, but the mandatory R4 variable paths were replaced by role-coded `variableDefinition`, so targeted migration is unavoidable while low-cost metadata and search-identity preservation still matter.

reasoning.thesisMd: `Evidence` is not removed, but it is also not a mostly stable resource. Every valid R4 Evidence instance has `exposureBackground`, and R6 has no such path; R6 instead represents population, exposure, outcome, comparator, and covariate concepts through repeatable `variableDefinition` entries with required role codes and observed/intended references. That makes an explicit resource-level transform necessary for real R4 instances, even before optional relationship and metadata removals are considered.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is a same-resource, targeted content-model remodel. R4's direct `exposureBackground`, `exposureVariant`, and `outcome` EvidenceVariable references must be classified into R6 variable roles, with policy for observed versus intended variables and for the R6 allowance of `Group` targets. R4 `relatedArtifact` must be mapped into the different `relatesTo.type`/`target[x]` backbone, and several optional metadata fields need preservation policy. R6 also adds statistics, certainty, assertion, synthesis type, and study design, which do not break R4-to-R6 validation but make down-conversion and bidirectional synchronization nontrivial.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the central variable transform is already unavoidable, preserving every old field name has less leverage than publishing high-quality migration rules. Still, the resource identity remains stable and the redesign is not so dominant that avoidable breaks should be dismissed. Low-cost deprecated metadata fields, explicit `relatedArtifact` mapping, and legacy SearchParameter canonical aliases can reduce churn without blocking the R6 Evidence model. The right posture is therefore to expect a targeted migration program while preserving compatibility where it is cheap, non-duplicative, or conformance-critical.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest avoidable local issue is the removal of optional metadata such as `shortTitle`, `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `effectivePeriod`, and `topic`; retaining them as deprecated optional elements would preserve old instances at low base-model cost. Keeping R4 `exposureBackground`/`exposureVariant`/`outcome` beside `variableDefinition` is only a partial alternative because it creates duplicate authoritative variable representations and consistency rules. Keeping `relatedArtifact` alongside `relatesTo` has similar duplicate-relationship tradeoffs, so it is more a mapping concern than an obvious low-cost preservation win.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The one direct behavior finding affects Evidence through SearchParameter canonical identity consolidation. The same query codes may remain usable, but systems that key CapabilityStatement support, generators, tests, or registries by canonical SearchParameter URL can see Evidence searches as missing or different. That deserves transition aliases or equivalence guidance. The 11 shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` operation and special-search findings are real platform issues but were not counted as Evidence-specific migration drivers.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's broad result: `Partial` major migration, `moderate-targeted-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. The important reason is not the raw count of three hard breaks; it is that the one mandatory R4 Evidence content path is gone, forcing a transform for every unchanged R4 instance, while the same resource identity and low R4 maturity keep the conclusion short of a full migration-dominates or removed-resource posture.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural differences because they come directly from the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions. Confidence is lower for prevalence and exact mapping policy because no official Evidence R4-to-R6 ConceptMap, StructureMap, migration guide, representative instance corpus, or full terminology expansion was available, and the R6 source is ballot4.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 population/exposure/outcome references were removed and remodeled as R6 variableDefinition entries
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the resource-level migration driver. R4 made `exposureBackground` mandatory and used direct variable reference paths, while R6 replaces that shape with role-coded `variableDefinition` entries. Even with FMM 0, unchanged R4 instances fail R6 validation and migration can require domain policy for roles, observed/intended distinctions, covariates, and Group versus EvidenceVariable targets.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds statistics, certainty, assertion, and study characterization that R4 Evidence cannot carry structurally
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This does not make old R4 Evidence instances invalid because the added R6 content is optional. It does, however, define the broader R6 Evidence model and makes reverse conversion lossy for statistics, certainty, sample sizes, model characteristics, and assertions. It should be handled by explicit downgrade/loss policy rather than by constraining the R6 model to the early R4 shape.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 relatedArtifact was removed from Evidence and replaced by a different relatesTo backbone
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 instances using `relatedArtifact` become invalid in R6, and citation/display/resource/url details do not map one-to-one into `relatesTo.type` plus `target[x]`. The R6 relationship model is coherent enough that retaining both fields is not clearly low cost, but the mapping is important for provenance, citation, audit, and repository behavior.

findingConsiderations.title: Several R4 metadata elements were removed with no direct R6 Evidence successor
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This remains the clearest low-cost compatibility preservation candidate. The removed optional fields are independent metadata rather than duplicate scientific variable or relationship representations, so retaining them as deprecated base elements or defining explicit same-fidelity successors would reduce validation and data-loss churn with limited downside.

findingConsiderations.title: Evidence.status is optional in R6 but was required in R4
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a relaxation for R4-to-R6 validation, not an old-valid/new-invalid break. Reverse conversion needs a policy when R6 omits `status`, but R6 supplies missing-value semantics and R4 already has an `unknown` publication-status code, so this is a local converter chore rather than a standards compatibility concern.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This direct Evidence behavior finding is not an instance-shape break, but it can break conformance metadata, generated clients, registries, and tests that compare search support by canonical SearchParameter URL. Legacy per-resource canonical aliases or explicit equivalence rules look relatively low cost and valuable during transition.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared `Resource` operation change can affect generic Evidence clients in the broader ecosystem, but it is not specific to the Evidence resource model and was not used to decide the resource-level migration shape.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search-parameter metadata issue applies to `Resource`/`DomainResource` generally. It is relevant background for platform migration but should be handled in shared behavior review rather than counted as an Evidence-specific break.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish an explicit R4 Evidence to R6 Evidence migration guide or StructureMap for `exposureBackground`, `exposureVariant`, and `outcome` into `variableDefinition.variableRole`, including observed/intended policy, covariates, Group targets, and reverse-conversion limits.
Revisit the removed optional metadata fields and either retain deprecated `shortTitle`, `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `effectivePeriod`, and `topic` or provide clear same-fidelity replacement mappings.

Define authoritative `relatedArtifact` to `relatesTo` mappings, including treatment of citation, label, display, URL, document, resource, relationship type terminology, and cases that cannot round-trip.
Provide transition guidance or deprecated aliases for Evidence-related per-resource SearchParameter canonical URLs that were consolidated into CanonicalResource/MetadataResource definitions.

caveats: No official Evidence R4-to-R6 ConceptMap, StructureMap, migration note, or change rationale was available in the supplied inputs.
No representative R4 Evidence instance corpus was supplied, so prevalence of optional metadata and relatedArtifact use is estimated from model centrality rather than measured deployment.
Terminology expansions and detailed value-set mappings for variable roles and artifact relationship types were not fully reviewed here.
The R6 input package is 6.0.0-ballot4, so final R6 content could change.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context and not scored as Evidence-specific findings.
